newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Jan-May operational deficit 0.36 pct of GDP.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Jan-May operational deficit 0.36 pct of GDP.

text.p: Brazil's federal government posted an operational deficit of 1.253 billion reais in the first five months of 1997, equivalent to 0.36 percent of gross domestic product, the National Treasury said Wednesday.
The operational deficit in the month of May was 627 million reais, the treasury said in a statement.

Brazil's primary account, which unlike the operational figure excludes debt servicing costs, posted a 632 million-real surplus in May, taking the surplus for the first five months of the year to 4.051 billion reais, or 1.18 percent of GDP.
Government officials have said they hope to finish 1997 with a 1.5 percent surplus in the primary account.

Receipts during the first five months of the year totalled 44.208 billion reais, and non-debt-related expenditure 40.157 billion reais. Debt costs during the period totalled 5.304 billion reais, the treasury said.

Brazil's nominal deficit, which includes debt payments and adjusts for foreign exchange fluctuations, was 627 million reais in May and 1.294 billion reais, or 1.88 percent of GDP, in the January-May period.
In the first five months of 1996, Brazil's treasury posted an operational deficit of 0.14 percent of GDP, a primary surplus of 1.03 percent, and a nominal deficit of 1.77 percent.
Total National Treasury debt in May stood at 136.528 billion reais, or 16.5 percent of GDP, of which 57.862 billion reais was in foreign debt, the statement said.

The treasury said it spent 1.55 billion reais generated by the privatization of mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce to buy debt from the market, reducing its stock of outstanding securitized paper to 118.453 billion reais, down 0.2 percent from April.
